move: watch face ticks: second hand snaps twice with elastic, digital time flips, activity rings sweep
how: A CSS smartwatch (band, brushed case, crown, black screen) whose screen holds a digital time, an SVG analog face with 60 generated tick marks and three hands, three activity rings and a heart-rate line. Over the 2s loop the second hand snaps 6deg twice (at 1% and 51%) with elastic.out(1.2,.35) over 0.18s, each snap swapping the digital seconds text and scaling it 1.12->1 (power2.out); the minute and hour hands crawl linearly. The rings drawSVG from 0% to 78/62/90% with power3.out over 1.2s, staggered 0.1s, then at 78% all erase to '100% 100%' with power3.in and a 0.05s stagger. The heart glyph beats scale 1.5 then back every 0.83s (72 BPM). The crown bobs y -6 in yoyo pairs.
adapt: Change the time string and seconds start, the ring percentages and colours (#ff375f/#a4ff3c/#0af), the BPM text, and the case and band colours. Keep the 0.18s elastic tick snap and the 0.83s heartbeat cadence.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the watch markup, generates the 60 ticks and sets the initial hand rotations; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with ticks at 0.01D and 0.51D, rings 0-0.6D and erase at 0.78D. Scope '#dg', '#ticks', '.sh', '.mh', '.hh', '.r1-3' to el and rename the ids; the case and band sizes are absolute pixels for a 1080 stage.
caveats: second hand ends 12deg ahead and the digital text two seconds later than frame 0, so the loop jumps back
rings erase to a state visually equal to their start, hands do not
layout is absolute pixels for a 1080x1080 stage
